newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel condemns "criminal steps" by government.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel condemns "criminal steps" by government.

text.p: A spokesman for the group that held hostages in the Japanese embassy residence in Lima accused President Alberto Fujimori's government of taking "criminal steps" by storming the building on Tuesday.

Isaac Velazco, spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), said in an interview from Germany with CNN that the rebels had known there was a 50 percent chance of a military raid but the government's action came as a surprise.
"The present regime has taken criminal steps and has acted in a criminal fashion by this action," he said, calling the government troops "death squads".
Peruvian troops stormed the residence to end a four-month standoff that started when MRTA rebels seized the building and took hostages during a diplomatic cocktail party on Dec. 17.
Local radio said all rebels holding the building and one of the 72 hostages were killed in Tuesday's raid.
